legend.priority: P0 = decides access, permissions, session, plan/entitlement, money, or holds credentials. P1 = everything else.
legend.tenant: org / org+user = the key contains the organisation id (and user id where the value is per user); global = same value for everyone, with a written reason; id-unique = the key is a random globally unique id; per-session = browser memory of one person.
legend.layers: redis, process (in-process memory), request (per request), next (Next.js caches), http (Cache-Control / ETag), client (TanStack Query), browser (storage), database (cache table).

caches.name: RBAC grant set per user
caches.what: The merged permission grants (allow/deny and record scope) of one user in one workspace, as JSON.

bound.note: One key per user per roles version; old versions expire on their own.

invalidation.trigger: Any role, grant or membership change: roles.service.ts (2 sites), users.service.ts, members.service.ts (2 sites).
invalidation.mechanism: RbacService.bumpRolesVersion() raises organizations.roles_version and rewrites rbac:version:${orgId}; the grant key name contains the version, so every old grant set is simply never read again.

caches.stampede: none: N parallel misses each load the grants from Postgres (measured in stampede.spec.ts for the sibling gate cache).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Redis error = miss: version read falls back to Postgres, grants are loaded from Postgres. A cache-write error is logged and ignored. No stale grant is ever served because Redis was down.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Every process, at once, after a successful bump. If both the DELETE and the SET of the version key fail (Redis down while an admin saves), bumpRolesVersion throws and the old version stays cached until its TTL: at most 600 s.
staleWindow.note: Measured against a real Redis in rbac-real-redis.spec.ts.

caches.hitMissPoint: rbac.service.ts grantsForUser: the `if (cached)` branch is a hit; falling through to loadGrants is a miss.

caches.name: RBAC roles version per workspace
caches.what: The integer organizations.roles_version, used to name the grant keys (R01).
caches.ttl: 600 s (Lua SET ... EX, never moves the version backwards)

invalidation.mechanism: bumpRolesVersion(): DEL with 3 retries, then Lua RAISE_VERSION (only raises).

caches.stampede: none (a miss reads one row from Postgres).
caches.hitMissPoint: rbac.service.ts rolesVersion / readCached (Lua returns false for a missing version).

caches.name: Platform operator permission names
caches.what: The permission names of one platform operator (staff of the product company, not a workspace user).

tenant.reason: Platform operators belong to no workspace; the operator id is globally unique.

invalidation.trigger: Operator role or permission change in platform-roles / platform-permissions services.
invalidation.mechanism: Version key `prbac:version` is raised; old names stop being read.

caches.name: Account gate state per user
caches.what: Whether a signed-in user is suspended, must verify email, enrol MFA or change password; plus is_admin / is_owner.

invalidation.trigger: Email verified, MFA enabled/disabled, password changed, user suspended or removed, invitation accepted (login, recovery, account, mfa, invitations, users, members services call gates.invalidate).
invalidation.mechanism: AccountGateService.invalidate(orgId, userId) = DEL; invalidateAll() = SCAN auth:gate:* + UNLINK on a policy change.

caches.stampede: none: parallel misses each run the SQL (stampede.spec.ts).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Redis read error = miss = compute from Postgres. Write error logged and ignored.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: The user themself and every process, if the writer did not call invalidate (e.g. a direct SQL change).

caches.name: Workspace suspended verdict
caches.what: true/false: is this workspace suspended by the platform.

invalidation.trigger: Platform inbox suspends / unsuspends a workspace.
invalidation.mechanism: OrgSuspensionService.invalidate(orgId): DEL now and again 1.5 s later (closes the race with a request that re-cached the old value).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Redis error = miss = Postgres read. If Postgres also fails the request is LET THROUGH (documented fail-open, ADR-0019): the suspension is durable and the next successful read enforces it.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Every process; 1.5 s extra for the recheck.

caches.hitMissPoint: org-suspension.service.ts isSuspended: `cached !== null` is a hit.

caches.name: Partner agent active flag
caches.what: 1/0: is this partner agent still active (partner tokens have no session row, so this is their revocation).

invalidation.trigger: An agent is deactivated. PartnerAgentStatusService.invalidate() exists but has NO caller in apps/api (no code path in this API changes partner_agents.status), so today only the TTL applies.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Closed mode (production default): Redis error = 503. Open mode: read Postgres, which is authoritative.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: The deactivated agent, on every instance.
staleWindow.note: invalidate() is unused: recorded as open risk R-64-02.

caches.name: Platform token epoch (mirror)
caches.what: The platform-wide token epoch; bumping it signs everybody out. Postgres (platform_settings) is the truth, Redis is a mirror.

tenant.reason: One number for the whole platform; not tenant data.

caches.ttl: none on purpose (durable mirror: a flushed Redis is refilled from Postgres, never reset to 0)

invalidation.mechanism: SET after the Postgres write; the bumping process also refreshes its own in-process copy.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Redis error = Postgres value; Redis miss refills with SET NX.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Other processes read the epoch through a 5 s in-process copy (M02).

caches.ttlException: Deliberately has no TTL: it is the mirror of a durable setting.

caches.name: Emergency send-halt mirror
caches.what: 1/0: has an operator halted all outbound sending.

tenant.reason: One platform-wide switch, not tenant data: it halts sending for every workspace.

invalidation.mechanism: SET of the mirror; Postgres setting is the truth.

caches.name: Session revocation and activity state
caches.what: Tombstone of a revoked session, last-activity time (idle timeout), session-cap marker. Authoritative for "is this access token still allowed".

tenant.reason: sid is a random uuid, globally unique; the value holds no tenant data.

caches.ttl: revoked: 16 min (access-token life + 60 s); activity 7 d (staff) / 24 h (operators); cap marker 31 d / 24 h

invalidation.trigger: Sign-out, revoke, password reset, concurrent-session eviction, idle expiry.
invalidation.mechanism: SessionService.tombstone(sid) = SET NX EX; if the SET fails the sid stays in an in-process pending list (M07) and the guard refuses it.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Closed mode (production default): a Redis error on the session check = 503. Open mode: the 15-minute access token bounds the exposure. Covered by test/unit/auth-registration-security/jwt-guard-partner-and-redis.spec.ts and item #18.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: No staleness: a tombstone is written before the revoke call returns.

caches.name: Impersonation ended tombstone
caches.what: An operator act-as session was ended; its token must fail on every instance.

tenant.reason: The key is a random impersonation session uuid, globally unique; the value is the flag 1.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Other instances, through the 5 s open-check copy (M05).

caches.name: Analytics series result
caches.what: Rows of a dashboard metric series for one workspace and one query.
caches.ttl: Caller supplies ttlSeconds (<= 0 disables the cache)
caches.stampede: in-process single-flight: parallel identical calls share one run (stampede.spec.ts).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Read/write errors are logged and ignored; the answer is computed.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Dashboards may be as old as the caller-chosen TTL.
staleWindow.note: TTL is chosen per call site, not documented in one place.

caches.name: Campaign / broadcast summary
caches.what: Computed delivery summary of one campaign or broadcast.

caches.name: SMS number lookup verdict
caches.what: Carrier lookup of a phone number ("check a number before you text it"); only successful verdicts are kept.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Read error = miss; write error ignored.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Staff using the lookup tool: a number that changed carrier shows the old carrier for up to 90 days.
staleWindow.note: No documented window; informational tool only.

caches.name: Knowledge-base query embedding
caches.what: The vector for a search question (binary).

tenant.reason: Content-addressed: the value is a pure function of (model, question text), so a reader of another workspace can only fetch the vector of a question it typed itself. Tenant isolation does not apply; the cost is shared, which is intended.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Errors ignored; the embedding is requested again.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Nobody: the value never changes for the same input.

caches.name: Translation result
caches.what: A translated text (and, for 60 s, a failed attempt).

tenant.reason: Content-addressed on (language, routing policy, md5 of the text); a reader can only fetch the translation of a text it submitted. Recommendation: use sha256 instead of md5.

invalidation.mechanism: Expiry. A residency / lockdown change changes `scope`, so the old answers are not read.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: RedisTranslationCache swallows errors; the provider is called.

caches.name: Active UI languages
caches.what: List of enabled interface languages.

tenant.reason: The list of interface languages is the same for every workspace (a platform setting).

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Everyone; 0 s if the admin path deleted the key.

caches.name: Booking page theme
caches.what: The look of a public booking page.

invalidation.trigger: Theme saved, picture uploaded/removed, theme chosen (booking-page-themes.service.ts, 4 sites).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Read error = miss; write/drop errors logged.

caches.name: WABA groups eligibility
caches.what: Whether a WhatsApp Cloud number may use groups (1/0).

invalidation.trigger: None except overwrite on a refusal.

caches.name: WhatsApp uploaded media id
caches.what: The id Meta gave an uploaded file, so the same file is not uploaded again.

invalidation.mechanism: Expiry; Meta ids expire on their side.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: "A cache that is down never fails a send": read error = miss, write error ignored.

caches.name: Idempotent response replay
caches.what: The first response to a request that carried an Idempotency-Key, replayed on a retry.

invalidation.trigger: None: the point is that it does not change.
invalidation.mechanism: A different actor with the same key gets its own entry (suffix); a different body on the same slot is a 409.

caches.stampede: SET NX reserves the key: parallel identical requests get a 409 instead of running twice.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Redis error on the reservation: the request is not executed (error propagates). A write error after success is logged.

caches.name: Storefront checkout idempotency
caches.what: First response to a public checkout with an Idempotency-Key.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Reservation error = request fails (never a double order).

caches.name: Channel dispatch result
caches.what: Result of sending one message, so a retry with the same client reference does not send twice.

caches.name: Conversation "seen" marker
caches.what: Which users looked at a conversation in the last minute (suppresses duplicate notifications).

tenant.anchor: const key = (orgId: number, userId: number, conversationUuid: string)

caches.name: Notification and AI copilot short state
caches.what: Chat history (2 h) and a pending confirmation (10 min) of the AI copilot for one user.

tenant.anchor: private historyKey(orgId: number, userId: number | null)

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Errors propagate for history writes (user sees an error).

caches.name: Mail bounced-address flag
caches.what: This address bounced; do not mail it.
caches.ttl: MAIL_BOUNCE_BLOCK_DAYS x 86400 s (days, set by the bounce handler)

invalidation.trigger: clearBounced(orgId, address) when the address recovers.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: "mail limits failed open": a Redis error lets the mail through.

caches.name: Active-worker and platform health probes
caches.what: A probe key and the outbox sample for the operator health page.

tenant.reason: Platform plumbing, no tenant data.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: A failing probe is the health signal.

caches.name: Payment-gateway plan cache table
caches.what: The plan id a payment gateway created for an (account, currency, amount, interval): created once, reused.
caches.key: gateway_plan_cache (gateway, account_hash, currency, amount_minor, interval_unit, interval_count)

tenant.reason: Platform billing (the product company's own gateways); account_hash separates gateway accounts.

invalidation.trigger: None: a gateway plan id does not change; a deleted plan at the provider would need manual repair.

caches.name: Realtime audience (who may receive an event)
caches.what: Users of a workspace who hold a permission, used to address realtime events.

invalidation.trigger: Role or team change this process knows about (invalidate(orgId)); other processes by TTL.

caches.stampede: a failed load is not remembered; parallel misses share nothing

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: No Redis. A person who must lose a room at once is evicted explicitly; joining a room always re-reads live grants (room-access.service.ts).

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Staff receiving events for conversations they lost access to; the REST fetch re-checks.

caches.name: Platform epoch local copy
caches.what: The token epoch number.

tenant.reason: One number for the whole platform (the token epoch); not tenant data.

caches.name: Platform settings snapshot
caches.what: All platform_settings rows (auth policy, limits, switches).

tenant.reason: Platform settings (auth policy, limits, switches); the same for every workspace.

invalidation.trigger: Any write through the service (7 sites) calls invalidate().

caches.name: Plan grace days
caches.what: billing.grace_days.

tenant.reason: billing.grace_days is one platform setting, not per workspace.

caches.name: Impersonation "still open" check
caches.what: Whether an operator act-as session is still open.

tenant.reason: Keyed by a random impersonation session uuid, globally unique; holds the operator session facts, not workspace records.

caches.name: Trial gate "not expired" verdict
caches.what: A workspace's trial has not run out (so every route is allowed).

invalidation.trigger: None: expiry only. A trial that ends is noticed within 5 s.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: An error resolving the plan lets the request through (documented).

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Workspace staff whose trial just expired.

caches.name: Pending session revocations
caches.what: Sessions revoked while the Redis tombstone could not be written.

tenant.reason: Keyed by a random session uuid (sid), globally unique; the value is an expiry time.

bound.note: Entries expire and are removed when Redis confirms. NOT capped on purpose: dropping an entry would un-revoke a session.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: This map is the fail-closed fallback itself.

caches.name: Consent settings per workspace
caches.what: Compiled opt-in / opt-out keywords and the consent switches.

invalidation.trigger: Save in the saving process; other processes by TTL.

caches.name: Minor-contact rule per workspace
caches.what: What marketing may do with contacts flagged as minors.

caches.name: Notification preferences per workspace
caches.what: Owner toggles for notification types.

caches.name: Mail branding footer
caches.what: The footer appended to mails, per workspace.

invalidation.trigger: bustFooterCache() bumps Redis version counters (per workspace or platform); each process compares the version.
invalidation.mechanism: INCR of FooterKeys.* (durable counter, no TTL by design)

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Other processes if the version bump failed.

caches.name: Persona view and definition
caches.what: Resolved UI persona for a workspace and the persona definitions.
caches.ttl: 30 s views / definitions until changed, missing 5 s

invalidation.trigger: The key contains the row revision, so a change is a new key.

caches.name: Calendar connection row (Google, Microsoft)
caches.what: The workspace's calendar connection including encrypted tokens (Microsoft: same, in microsoft-calendar-tokens.service.ts).

invalidation.trigger: invalidate(orgId) on connect / disconnect / refresh failure.

caches.name: Calendar free/busy answer
caches.what: Busy intervals of the workspace calendar (Microsoft: same file pattern).

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: A failed read marks the workspace failedAt and the booking is not blocked.

caches.name: Calendar provider preference
caches.what: Which calendar provider the workspace uses.

caches.name: Webhook-forward target
caches.what: Delivery settings of one platform webhook-forward target (includes the encrypted auth header).

tenant.reason: Row id of a platform-level table (webhook_forward_targets); not tenant data.

invalidation.trigger: invalidate(id?) after edit in the editing process.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Other processes: a deleted/switched-off target may still get a delivery.

caches.name: Wallet "send ok" short-cut
caches.what: This workspace could afford a send a moment ago.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: A drained wallet can still send for 3 s.

caches.name: Message price cards
caches.what: Meta price per market and category, and the platform rate card.

tenant.reason: Platform price list, same for every workspace.

bound.note: One entry per currency; cleared on import.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: Other processes after a price import.

caches.name: Currency table
caches.what: Currencies and exchange data.

tenant.reason: The currency table is platform-wide and the same for every workspace.

caches.name: Module registry snapshot
caches.what: Which modules / add-ons are on.

tenant.reason: The module registry (which add-ons are on) is platform-wide, not per workspace.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: Failure yields "no contributions" and the next call retries.

caches.name: Provider router and WhatsApp provider resolver snapshots
caches.what: Routing rows for translation providers (5 s) and WhatsApp provider list (15 s).

tenant.reason: Routing configuration of translation and WhatsApp providers; platform-wide.

caches.name: API docs and health snapshots
caches.what: Generated OpenAPI document (60 s) and platform health (3 s).

tenant.reason: Platform data, no tenant content.

caches.name: Inbox channel and subject lookups
caches.what: uuid of the inbox channel of a device and thread subjects (also history-import.sink.ts channels).

caches.name: Display-id reservations
caches.what: A block of 100 reserved display numbers per workspace and module.

bound.note: an evicted block leaves a gap in the numbers, which is accepted by design

caches.name: Time-zone helpers
caches.what: Intl.DateTimeFormat objects and valid-zone answers (also ics-feed-parser.ts validZones, sla-calculator.ts formatters).

tenant.reason: Pure function of the zone name.

bound.note: validZones 1000; the zone name in a calendar feed is attacker-controlled

caches.name: Throttle markers
caches.what: Last "touch" per workspace (activity.service), last realtime wallet publish (wallet-realtime.publisher), recent PQL calls per user (pql.service).

caches.name: In-flight sharing and token refresh
caches.what: Maps of promises for calls in progress: analytics inFlight, uploader inFlight, token refreshing (google, microsoft, mail, conferencing), meeting running. Each entry is removed in a `finally` when the call ends.

tenant.reason: The analytics key carries the workspace id (an:v1:${q.orgId}); token-refresh maps are keyed by workspace id; the media uploader key carries the content hash and orgId.

bound.note: bounded by concurrency, not by history

caches.name: Memory fallbacks of Redis caches
caches.what: MemoryUploadedMediaCache and MemoryTranslationStores: used in tests or when no Redis is bound.

caches.name: Google OIDC signing keys
caches.what: Google's published JWKS used to verify Pub/Sub push tokens.

tenant.reason: Google public signing keys; the same for everyone and not secret.

caches.ttl: Cache-Control max-age from Google; unknown kid re-read at most every 2 s

bound.note: replaced as a whole on each fetch

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: "Fails closed: with no keys available nothing verifies."

caches.name: Auth prefetch
caches.what: The Redis reads of the gate, suspension and RBAC checks, started together by JwtAuthGuard and handed to each check once. Not a cache of decisions.

tenant.reason: Lives in the request context of one request; also checked for the same org and user.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: A failed read is replaced by the consumer's own fresh read.

caches.name: React cache() in the web app
caches.what: getRequestSession = cache(getSession), loadRegistrationConfig, loadPasswordPolicy: React's per-request memo for server rendering.

tenant.reason: React cache() lives for one server request only.

caches.name: Next.js data cache for platform pages
caches.what: fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 300 } }) for manifest.webmanifest, team-inbox-manifest, sitemap.xml, robots.txt (300 s) the public API reference page (60 s) and the public site settings (30 s): public platform pages, the same for everybody; none forwards a cookie or Authorization.

tenant.reason: Public platform pages; no tenant or user data; no credentials forwarded.

caches.name: Next.js response headers
caches.what: headers(): every page `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private, max-age=0` where listed (NO_STORE_PAGES, /q/*, /book/*); /sw.js always revalidated; the rest follow Next defaults (dynamic pages are not cached).

tenant.reason: These are response headers, not stored data; nothing is cached on the server.

caches.name: Web frame-policy memo
caches.what: Frame-ancestors policy of a published form, per form key, in the Next server process.

tenant.reason: Public form definition; key is the public form route.

backingStoreFailure.behaviour: A failed fetch memoises null for 30 s.

caches.name: Default response cache header for credentialed requests
caches.what: Any API request that carries Authorization or a cookie gets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; paths in NO_STORE get `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private, max-age=0`. A controller may override.

tenant.reason: This is a response header, not stored data; nothing is cached on the server.

caches.name: Private browser cache for media
caches.what: `private, max-age=300` on chat media, email attachments, developer-API media, widget cover (private), team-chat file (private, 3600).

tenant.reason: Header; the response is for the authenticated caller and is `private`.

caches.name: Private immutable images with a version in the URL
caches.what: `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` + ETag on the avatar, workspace brand assets and the invoice logo. The URL carries `?v=<etag>`, so a new file is a new URL.

tenant.reason: `private`; per authenticated user or workspace, and the version is in the URL.

invalidation.trigger: A new upload changes the etag and therefore the URL.

caches.name: Public immutable assets (capability URLs)
caches.what: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on flow media (org uuid + random stored name), chatbot widget assets (flowId/slot?v=etag) and public booking pictures (uuid or brand-logo). Public on purpose: embedded on third-party pages.

tenant.reason: Public by design: the address is the credential (random uuid / stored name) and the content is meant for the public page.

invalidation.trigger: New upload = new name / etag in the URL.

caches.name: Public short-lived JSON and ETag
caches.what: `public, max-age=30` on the public form definition (+ ETag / 304), `public, max-age=60` on the workspace trust page and API docs, `public, max-age=30|300` on platform public settings, `no-cache, must-revalidate` on the chat widget script.

tenant.reason: Public pages of a published form / trust page; the URL names the workspace, content is intended to be public.

caches.name: TanStack Query defaults (staff web app)
caches.what: One QueryClient for the whole app: staleTime 30 s, gcTime = library default 5 min, retry on 5xx. Cached lists, settings, permissions of the signed-in user in browser memory.
caches.key: queryKey (mostly NOT containing the workspace or user)

tenant.reason: The cache is one per browser tab and is cleared on workspace switch (workspace-switcher.tsx) and, after fix D-64-05, on every sign-out (full page navigation). Keys do not carry org or user ids, so clearing on identity change is what makes it safe.

invalidation.trigger: Mutations call invalidateQueries; workspace switch clear(); sign-out full navigation.

staleWindow.whoReadsStale: The same person in the same tab (fresh for 30 s, then refetched; shown stale up to 5 min while refetching).

caches.name: Per-screen staleTime / gcTime overrides
caches.what: `staleTime: Infinity` for static reference data, `staleTime: 0` + `gcTime: 0` for secrets (QR, MFA setup), 5 s to 5 min for lists. Counts are in the report.

tenant.reason: Same as C01: one cache per browser tab, cleared on workspace switch and sign-out.

caches.name: Browser storage preferences
caches.what: localStorage / sessionStorage: UI preferences (columns, tabs, cookie consent) and sign-up form stage (non-secret). No tokens, no tenant records.

tenant.reason: Per browser; holds no tenant data or credentials.

redisFamilies.name: Sign-in, sign-up and MFA challenges
redisFamilies.keys: auth:mfa:*, auth:wschoice:*, auth:mfa-try:*, auth:signup*, auth:social:*, auth:mfa-setup:${orgId}:*, auth:wa-reg:*, auth:wa-login:*, auth:alert:${orgId}:*

tenant.reason: Keyed by the hash of a random one-time token (no tenant data in the key); where a person is named the key carries orgId (mfa-setup, alert).

redisFamilies.ttl: 5 to 30 min; sign-up stage up to 7 d
redisFamilies.failure: Closed (503) in production: a challenge that cannot be stored cannot be answered.

redisFamilies.name: Login lockouts and OTP / mail send counters
redisFamilies.keys: auth:lock:${orgId}:*, auth:ipfail:*, auth:acct-fail:${pool}:${orgId}:*, auth:known-nets:${pool}:${orgId}:*, auth:mfa-fail:*:${orgId}:*, auth:otp-phone:*, auth:send-min:${orgId}:*, auth:send-day:${orgId}:*

tenant.reason: Per-person keys carry orgId; per-address and per-phone counters are global by design (an attacker is not a tenant) and hold only numbers.

redisFamilies.ttl: window length (60 s to 90 d for known networks)
redisFamilies.failure: Closed in production (503), open elsewhere (platform failure mode).

redisFamilies.name: Public endpoint and API-key throttles
redisFamilies.keys: per IP / per public token / per workspace counters with a time bucket or an EXPIRE (apikey:authfail:*, ratelimit:apikey:*, link_hits:*, store_rl:*, ...)

tenant.reason: Public throttles are keyed by client address or public token (no tenant data); workspace-level ones carry orgId. Values are counters.

redisFamilies.ttl: 60 s to 2 d (all set atomically since D-64-01)
redisFamilies.failure: Open: a throttle protects against abuse; a Redis outage must not become an API outage (RateLimiter.degraded flag, logged).

redisFamilies.name: Public channel inbound throttles
redisFamilies.keys: line_hits:*, tg_hits:*, viber_hits:*, wechat_hits:*, wgt:hits:*, invoicing:rl:*, store_rl:*

tenant.reason: Keyed by the public webhook token or client address plus a one-minute bucket; the value is a counter.

redisFamilies.ttl: 120 s (set with the first hit in one transaction since D-64-01)

redisFamilies.name: Locks and leases
redisFamilies.keys: lock:* with a random owner token and PX / EX

tenant.reason: Names of jobs and per-device leases; the value is a random owner token.

redisFamilies.failure: A lock that cannot be taken means the job does not run (safe).

redisFamilies.name: Replay and duplicate markers
redisFamilies.keys: SET NX with an id from the provider (message id, order id, form submission id)

tenant.reason: Provider message ids are globally unique; where a tenant could collide the key carries orgId (wa:in:${orgId}:..., flr:gform:${orgId}:...).

redisFamilies.failure: Open for dedupe (a duplicate may be processed once more).

redisFamilies.name: Device runtime, inbox bridge and pairing state
redisFamilies.keys: wa:qr|code|status:${orgId}:${deviceId}, wa:cmd:*, inbox sent/inbound-media keys, history tallies, worker heartbeat

tenant.reason: Device state carries orgId + deviceId; command results and heartbeats are keyed by a random id.

redisFamilies.failure: Pairing and sending degrade; no authorisation decision depends on them.

redisFamilies.name: Realtime tickets and presence
redisFamilies.keys: single-use realtime ticket (random), presence keys with orgId and userId

tenant.reason: A realtime ticket is a random single-use token whose value holds the claims; presence keys carry orgId and userId.

redisFamilies.name: WhatsApp Cloud throughput governor
redisFamilies.keys: per phone-number-id second / minute counters and config hashes

tenant.reason: Meta phone-number-id is globally unique; values are counters and platform config. One hash (govKeys.global) is durable by design.

redisFamilies.name: Cache-version counters (durable)

tenant.reason: A counter per workspace and one for the platform.

redisFamilies.ttl: none on purpose: a version counter must not reset (INCR only goes up)
redisFamilies.failure: A failed bump is not an error: the cache also expires on its own.

redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/auth/sessions/epoch.service.ts: Durable mirror of a Postgres setting (R07): a flushed Redis is refilled from Postgres; an expiring epoch would silently re-validate revoked tokens.
redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/auth/security/branding-footer.se: Version counter (S10): INCR only; a counter that expires would reset to 1 and make old cached footers look current.
redisNoTtlAllowed.infra/providers/whatsapp-cloud-api-waba/: govKeys.global hash is the governor's durable platform config; every other key in the file expires.
redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/node-bridge-runtime/runtime/grou: DECR undoes an INCR on a key that was created with an expiry in the same MULTI.
redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/platform-infrastructure/observab: Sorted set of live workers; members older than the window are removed on every write and the set holds one member per worker.
redisNoTtlAllowed.realtime/visibility-presence.service.ts: Sorted set; EXPIRE is set in the same MULTI.
redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/whatsapp-devices-baileys/history: Tallies are given EXPIRE once the import ends (TALLY_TTL_S); during a run they must not expire.
redisNoTtlAllowed.modules/auth/security/account-attack.ser: SADD followed by EXPIRE in the same try block; the set is trimmed by SPOP above MAX_KNOWN_NETWORKS.
